backlog.spec: In _repair, instead of picking the single largest overlap each step, scan the pairs in a random order from the seed's rng and fix every overlapping pair in that order by proportional shrink, looping until no overlap remains or 200 passes are used. Break ties at random. This changes which circles absorb the shrink and can keep more total radius than the greedy largest-overlap rule, with no change to the optimiser.
backlog.title: Random-order repair with max-overlap ties

backlog.spec: Stack the three changes that each scored slightly better than the incumbent. Give _solve_once an optional argument x0 and let solve choose the start type for each restart with the seeded rng: (a) with probability 1/4 the plain uniform start; (b) with probability 1/4 a perimeter-ring start: about 16 centres evenly spaced along a square ring at distance 0.1 from the walls with Gaussian jitter of sd 0.02, the remaining centres uniform in [0.25, 0.75]^2, radii INIT_RADIUS; (c) with probability 1/4 a uniform centre start whose radii follow a shuffled power-law profile, r_k proportional to k^-0.5 for k = 1..n, rescaled to mean INIT_RADIUS and clipped to [0.02, 0.1]; (d) with probability 1/4, once a best packing exists, an affine-strain shake of the best centres: map c to 0.5 + (c - 0.5) @ A with A = I + E, E a random 2x2 matrix with entries N(0, 0.05), clip to [0.05, 0.95], radii reset to INIT_RADIUS (before a best packing exists use type a). All starts then run the unchanged radius-cap continuation and repair.
backlog.title: Three-way mixture of the near-win restart types

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP stage, check the returned iterate for feasibility: all pair constraints and wall constraints at least -1e-9 and the sum of radii finite. If the stage's result is infeasible or res.status indicates a failure, keep the previous stage's feasible x rather than the failed iterate. Use the previous x for the next stage. This stops an unstable SLSQP stage from pushing a bad start into later caps and from being selected as best.
backlog.title: Feasibility guard on stage acceptance

backlog.spec: Give the continuation stages unequal SLSQP iteration budgets. Replace the single MAX_ITER with two constants: STAGE_ITER = 40 for every capped stage (cap < 1.0) and FINAL_ITER = 600 for the last free stage (cap = 1.0). In the loop pass options={'maxiter': STAGE_ITER if cap < 1.0 else FINAL_ITER}. The capped stages only need to move the configuration roughly; the final stage should run to true convergence instead of stopping at 200 iterations. Keep the cap list, the constraints and the repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Short capped stages, long final free stage

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, pass options={'maxiter': 40} to minimize for every capped stage (cap < 1.0) and options={'maxiter': 400} for the final cap=1.0 stage. Write it as maxiter = 400 if cap >= 1.0 else 40 inside the loop. The capped stages only need to steer the packing roughly. The final stage gets enough iterations to converge fully, and the restarts are cheaper overall.
backlog.title: Split SLSQP iteration budget: short capped stages, long free stage

backlog.spec: Add inequality constraints r[k] >= r[k+1] for k in 0..n-2 to the SLSQP constraint vector in cons, only for the cap stages, and sort the initial radii in descending order. This removes permutation symmetry among circles. Drop the ordering constraints in the last stage (cap=1.0) so the final optimum is unrestricted.
backlog.title: Radius-ordering symmetry breaking

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, after the cap loop finishes, call minimize once more with the same objective, the cap=1.0 constraint function, method SLSQP and maxiter MAX_ITER, starting from x. Then set x = res.x and return as before. Restarting SLSQP clears its BFGS Hessian approximation and its line-search state, which often lets it get a little further than a solver that has stalled. This adds a single extra stage and changes nothing else.
backlog.title: Second fresh free SLSQP stage per restart

backlog.spec: In the cap loop of _solve_once, before calling minimize for a cap below 1.0, check whether the cap would bind: if the current radii satisfy x[2*n:].max() < cap - 1e-6 and at least one stage has already been solved, skip all remaining capped stages and go straight to the final free stage (cap = 1.0). Implement with a simple `if cap < 1.0 and solved and x[2*n:].max() < cap - 1e-6: continue`. This removes the redundant SLSQP solves at high caps where the previous solution is already a local optimum, so more restarts fit in the time budget. No other change.
backlog.title: Skip cap stages that are not binding

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, change the cap list from np.arange(0.05, 0.4 + 1e-9, 0.02) + [1.0] (19 stages) to a coarser one: [0.05, 0.08, 0.11, 0.14, 0.18] + [1.0] (6 stages). Keep everything else identical. The aim is roughly three times as many restarts in the same CPU time while keeping the continuation effect in the radius range that matters (optimal radii lie around 0.07 to 0.14). Put the list in a module-level constant CAPS so it is easy to tune.
backlog.title: Coarser cap schedule for more restarts

backlog.spec: In solve, once a best packing exists, run half the restarts (rng.random() < 0.5) as reheats instead of random starts. Start from the best centres plus Gaussian noise with sd 0.02, clipped to [0.05, 0.95]. Set all radii to 0.05. Then run the full radius-cap continuation from that start (pass the start vector to _solve_once through an optional x0 argument). The other half stay uniform random restarts. Unlike plain perturbation, this lets the circles regrow their sizes from scratch while keeping the incumbent's spatial layout.
backlog.title: Cap-reheat of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Abandon unpromising restarts in the middle of the cap continuation. Keep in solve a list of the sum of radii that each earlier restart had right after a fixed checkpoint stage (the stage with cap closest to 0.11) and pass it to _solve_once. After that checkpoint stage, compute the current sum of radii; if at least 6 earlier values are recorded and the current value is below their median, return None immediately (solve then skips repair and comparison for that restart); in every case append the value to the list. Restarts that pass continue through the remaining caps and the free stage as now. This spends about half the late-stage SLSQP time only on the better half of the starts. Everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Stage-level racing of restarts

backlog.spec: After the first 5 plain restarts, on every third restart start SLSQP (with the cap continuation starting at cap=0.4 then 1.0 only) from a random one of the 8 dihedral images of the best packing's centres and radii, with small Gaussian noise (sd 0.01) on the centres. Keep the best result by sum of radii after repair.
backlog.title: Dihedral images of the best as restart seeds

backlog.spec: Change the settings INIT_LOW from 0.1 to 0.03 and INIT_RADIUS from 0.05 to 0.02. Change nothing else. Starting centres then cover nearly the whole square, including the border bands where many circles in good packings sit. The smaller initial radii start below the first cap of 0.05, so the first capped stage does real growth work instead of starting at the cap.
backlog.title: Wider centre spread and smaller initial radii

backlog.spec: Split the time budget into two phases in solve. For the first 55 percent of time_limit run the plain random restarts exactly as now. From then until TIME_FRACTION * time_limit, run only exploitation restarts from the best packing: take the best centres, apply a random affine strain c -> 0.5 + (c - 0.5) @ (I + E) with E a 2x2 matrix of N(0, 0.04) entries plus per-centre Gaussian jitter of sd 0.005, clip to [0.05, 0.95], reset radii to INIT_RADIUS, and run the full unchanged cap continuation (give _solve_once an optional x0 argument). Replace the best whenever the repaired sum of radii improves, so later shakes start from the new best. All randomness from the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Explore then exploit time split

backlog.spec: After _repair returns a valid packing, make one growth pass: for each circle in random order (rng from seed), set its radius to the largest value that keeps it inside the square and clear of all other circles given their current radii, i.e. r_i = min(wall distance, min_j(d_ij - r_j)). Repeat the pass until the total sum stops increasing by more than 1e-12, at most 5 passes. Then subtract SHRINK as before. This recovers slack left by the pairwise shrink, especially around rattlers, and does not change the SLSQP stage.
backlog.title: Greedy radius growth after repair

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the cap list list(np.arange(0.05, 0.4 + 1e-9, 0.02)) + [1.0] with list(np.arange(0.05, 0.4 + 1e-9, 0.05)) + [1.0], so there are 8 capped stages instead of 18, followed by the free stage. Change nothing else. Each restart becomes much cheaper, so more random restarts fit in the same TIME_FRACTION of the budget. This tests whether the gain from the continuation comes from having stages at all rather than from small steps.
backlog.title: Coarser cap ladder for more restarts

backlog.spec: In the cap continuation, give each circle its own cap instead of one shared cap. At the start of each restart, draw weights w = rng.permutation(np.linspace(0.6, 1.4, n)). In capped stages, replace the constraint cap - r with cap * w - r, where cap runs over the same ladder 0.05..0.4. Keep the final cap=1.0 stage unchanged, so its constraint is 1.0 - r. This breaks the size symmetry in the early stages, so that some circles are encouraged to grow large and others to stay small. That size mix is what good 26-circle packings have.
backlog.title: Per-circle heterogeneous radius caps

backlog.spec: Replace the linear cap grid np.arange(0.05, 0.4, 0.02) plus 1.0 with a geometric grid from 0.05 up to 0.2, then a linear grid from 0.2 to 0.4 with step 0.01, then 1.0. Radii of the 26-circle optimum are around 0.08 to 0.2, so most of the continuation should be spent in that band. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Geometric cap grid near the final radius scale

backlog.spec: For a random third of the restarts, build the start as a 5x5 grid of centres at spacing 0.2 offset by 0.1, add one extra centre at a random location, jitter all centres with Gaussian noise sd 0.03, and use initial radius 0.08. Other restarts stay uniform random. The cap continuation is applied as before.
backlog.title: Square-grid-with-defects starts

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the cap list with list(0.04 * 1.15 ** np.arange(17)) + [1.0], about 0.04 rising to roughly 0.38 in 17 steps. Steps are fine where the caps are small and the topology is decided, and coarse near the top where most constraints are already inactive. The number of stages stays close to the current 18, so the cost per restart is about the same.
backlog.title: Geometric cap ladder with fine early steps

memo:
All 40 slots (0-39) are used. Incumbent is still slot 8, the radius-cap SLSQP continuation: -2.6343, one run, never replicated (noise sd 0.0023). It is the only clear win (delta -0.0063). It improved per-restart SLSQP convergence.

Slots 39 (-2.6354), 28 (-2.6360) and 16 (-2.6354) came out lower than the incumbent. Their deltas are -0.0012, -0.0017 and -0.0012, which is within noise. Slots 10, 9 and 15 were neutral. Slots 13, 23, 31, 32 and 36 matched -2.6343 or came within 0.0003 of it.

Hurt: extra stages, other solvers (slots 24, 25), pair pruning (slot 18), start-shape tweaks (19, 20, 29, 30, 34, 35, 37), penalties (26, 27) and schedule priors (38).

Next: replicate slot 8, then replicate slots 28, 16 and 39 and stack the ones that hold. Tune the cap schedule. Avoid new penalties, solvers and start-shape changes.
